newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Agency upgrades Bahrain Middle East Bank's rating.
newsitem.headline: Agency upgrades Bahrain Middle East Bank's rating.

text.p: Capital Intelligence agency said on Tuesday it upgraded the long-term rating of Bahrain Middle East Bank (BMB) to BB+ from BB.
The Cyprus-based agency said the short-term rating remains unchanged at A-3 and the bank's outlook was stable.
Kuwait government-controlled Burgan Bank holds the majority share of BMB with a 28.6 percent stake. About 15,000 private investors hold the remaining shares.

A new management team in 1993 helped transform the bank's outlook, Capital Intelligence said. In May 1996, BMB completed one of the largest securitisations undertaken by a Middle East-based bank, with the formation of Global Diversified CBO Limited.
Income from trading and investment related activities has been diversified, leading to a dramatic rise in profitablity, especially in the last two years, said Capital Intelligence.

The bank, established in 1982, remains small by international standards, with total assets of US $646 million at end 1996. Capital Intelligence said BMB is strongly capitalised for the risks it undertakes, cushioning it against unforseen adverse general market developments or specific transactions that may go sour.

Concerns still exist regarding the bank's funding profile, but Capital Intelligence said the bank is currently examining ways of diversifying its funding sources and of lengthening the tenor of its liabilities.
